overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of how governments, companies, and international bodies are trying to govern AI. You'll be asked about the EU's risk levels, the US federal and state picture, China's measures, frontier safety frameworks, how commitments are checked, the two criticisms of self-governance, summits and declarations, scientific and treaty bodies, security competition, and military use.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: Under the EU's AI Act, the same sorting software is minimal risk when it filters spam and high risk when it ranks job applicants. What does this show about how the Act classifies AI?

options.html: It classifies by the age of the software
options.text: It classifies by the age of the software
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the European Union's risk-based law.

options.html: It classifies by the use the system is put to
options.text: It classifies by the use the system is put to
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The four levels sort uses. Employment is a listed high-risk area, so the level changes when the use does.

options.html: It classifies by the size of the company involved
options.text: It classifies by the size of the company involved
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the European Union's risk-based law.

options.html: It classifies by the country the developer is based in
options.text: It classifies by the country the developer is based in
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the European Union's risk-based law.

forms.stemHtml: As of October 2026, which statement describes the legal picture for AI in the United States?

options.html: One federal AI statute had replaced all state AI laws
options.text: One federal AI statute had replaced all state AI laws
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the United States.

options.html: No rules of any kind applied to AI systems
options.text: No rules of any kind applied to AI systems
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the United States.

options.html: No comprehensive federal statute; several state laws
options.text: No comprehensive federal statute; several state laws
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Federal direction came from executive orders, several states had passed their own laws, and Congress had not passed a statute preempting them.

options.html: State AI laws had been struck down by the courts
options.text: State AI laws had been struck down by the courts
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the United States.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these describe China's rules for generative AI as of October 2026? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: They are measures issued by state agencies
options.text: They are measures issued by state agencies
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The rules come from agencies, led by the Cyberspace Administration of China.

options.html: They require labels on AI-generated content
options.text: They require labels on AI-generated content
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Measures in effect since September 2025 require explicit labels and labels embedded in file data.

options.html: They sort uses of AI into four levels of risk
options.text: They sort uses of AI into four levels of risk
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on China.

options.html: They require training data from lawful sources
options.text: They require training data from lawful sources
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The 2023 measures require providers to use data and models that have lawful sources.

forms.stemHtml: In a company's safety framework, what is an if-then commitment?

options.html: A promise to follow whatever rules a regulator later sets
options.text: A promise to follow whatever rules a regulator later sets
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on frontier safety frameworks.

options.html: A promise to release a model if rivals release theirs
options.text: A promise to release a model if rivals release theirs
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on frontier safety frameworks.

options.html: A promise to apply safeguards if a threshold is reached
options.text: A promise to apply safeguards if a threshold is reached
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An if-then commitment ties a stated capability threshold to stated safeguards that must be in place before the developer goes further.

options.html: A promise to publish test results if a government asks
options.text: A promise to publish test results if a government asks
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on frontier safety frameworks.

forms.stemHtml: What do government safety institutes, outside evaluators, and employee whistleblowers have in common as ways of checking a company's safety commitments?

options.html: Each can order a company to stop a release
options.text: Each can order a company to stop a release
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how commitments are checked.

options.html: Each depends on access the company allows
options.text: Each depends on access the company allows
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Institutes rely on voluntary agreements, evaluators on the access they're given, and employees on contract terms and channels the company sets.

options.html: Each is required by an international treaty
options.text: Each is required by an international treaty
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how commitments are checked.

options.html: Each reports only to the company's own board
options.text: Each reports only to the company's own board
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how commitments are checked.

forms.stemHtml: Two groups criticize AI companies' safety commitments from opposite directions. Which statements belong to the regulatory-capture critique? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Safety rules cost large firms little and newcomers a lot
options.text: Safety rules cost large firms little and newcomers a lot
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The capture argument says incumbents can afford compliance, so rules built around their practices act as a barrier.

options.html: Warnings of danger are used to restrict open models
options.text: Warnings of danger are used to restrict open models
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Critics such as Andrew Ng argue that some large companies call AI dangerous in order to block open projects that compete with them.

options.html: Voluntary commitments loosen under competition
options.text: Voluntary commitments loosen under competition
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on each criticism of self-governance.

options.html: Only binding rules on every company will hold
options.text: Only binding rules on every company will hold
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on each criticism of self-governance.

forms.stemHtml: Countries at an AI summit sign a declaration recognizing risks from advanced AI. A year later one signer does nothing the declaration mentions. What consequence follows under the declaration?

options.html: The signer is fined by the summit's host
options.text: The signer is fined by the summit's host
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on summits and declarations.

options.html: The signer is removed from the United Nations
options.text: The signer is removed from the United Nations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on summits and declarations.

options.html: None, because a declaration is non-binding
options.text: None, because a declaration is non-binding
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A declaration creates no legal duty, and nothing happens to a signatory that ignores it.

options.html: The signer must submit to inspections
options.text: The signer must submit to inspections
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on summits and declarations.

forms.stemHtml: A country signs a framework convention on AI and never ratifies it. Is that country bound by the treaty?

options.html: Yes, because signing is the final step
options.text: Yes, because signing is the final step
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on scientific and treaty bodies.

options.html: No, because it hasn't ratified
options.text: No, because it hasn't ratified
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Ratification is a country's formal act of accepting a treaty as binding on itself. A country can sign and never ratify.

options.html: Yes, because all treaties bind every country
options.text: Yes, because all treaties bind every country
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on scientific and treaty bodies.

options.html: No, because treaties on AI can't be binding
options.text: No, because treaties on AI can't be binding
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on scientific and treaty bodies.

forms.stemHtml: Why does the belief that AI is a "race" make international limits on AI hard to agree?

options.html: Each side fears a rival won't keep the limit
options.text: Each side fears a rival won't keep the limit
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! If one side holds back and the other doesn't, the side that held back is worse off, so neither accepts a limit it can't confirm the other is keeping.

options.html: Races are forbidden under international law
options.text: Races are forbidden under international law
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on security competition.

options.html: Limits would make AI chips too cheap to control
options.text: Limits would make AI chips too cheap to control
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on security competition.

options.html: Most countries have no interest in AI at all
options.text: Most countries have no interest in AI at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on security competition.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements about autonomous weapons were accurate as of October 2026? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: No binding international ban on them existed
options.text: No binding international ban on them existed
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The Red Cross and the UN Secretary-General asked for a treaty by 2026, and no treaty was shown to have been concluded.

options.html: US policy permitted them, subject to senior review
options.text: US policy permitted them, subject to senior review
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The US directive requires appropriate levels of human judgment over the use of force and permits autonomous weapons after approval.

options.html: Every UN member had voted for a treaty banning them
options.text: Every UN member had voted for a treaty banning them
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on military use and autonomous weapons.

options.html: Most states had voted for further UN work on them
options.text: Most states had voted for further UN work on them
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Resolutions passed with 166 votes in 2024 and 164 in 2025, with several military powers voting against or abstaining.

forms.stemHtml: A company offers a chatbot on a shop's website in the EU. Later, a bank uses the same chatbot to decide who qualifies for credit. Under the AI Act's approach, what happens to its risk level?

options.html: It stays the same, since the software is unchanged
options.text: It stays the same, since the software is unchanged
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the European Union's risk-based law.

options.html: It falls, since banks are already regulated
options.text: It falls, since banks are already regulated
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the European Union's risk-based law.

options.html: It becomes a banned practice in every case
options.text: It becomes a banned practice in every case
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the European Union's risk-based law.

options.html: It rises, since the use has changed
options.text: It rises, since the use has changed
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Risk-based regulation sets heavier duties for uses that could do more harm. Deciding access to an essential service is a listed high-risk use.

forms.stemHtml: A senator proposes a federal AI law that would stop state AI laws on the same subject from applying. What is this effect called?

options.html: Preemption
options.text: Preemption
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Preemption is the rule that a federal law overrides state laws on the same subject.

options.html: Ratification
options.text: Ratification
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the United States.

options.html: Enforcement
options.text: Enforcement
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the United States.

options.html: Revocation
options.text: Revocation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the United States.

forms.stemHtml: Under China's 2023 measures, a generative AI service that can shape public opinion faces further duties. Which are they? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A security assessment
options.text: A security assessment
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Services with public opinion properties or the capacity for social mobilization must carry out a security assessment.

options.html: A vote of approval by the legislature
options.text: A vote of approval by the legislature
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on China.

options.html: Filing its algorithm with the regulator
options.text: Filing its algorithm with the regulator
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Algorithm filing is the registration of a service's algorithm with the regulator.

options.html: Publishing its model for anyone to download
options.text: Publishing its model for anyone to download
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on China.

forms.stemHtml: A developer's framework says that if a model can substantially help someone carry out a cyberattack, the developer will add specified security measures before releasing it. Which part of this is the capability threshold?

options.html: The model's ability to help with a cyberattack
options.text: The model's ability to help with a cyberattack
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A capability threshold is a specified level of ability at which a model is judged to require stronger protections. The security measures are the safeguard.

options.html: The security measures the developer will add
options.text: The security measures the developer will add
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on frontier safety frameworks.

options.html: The date on which the model is released
options.text: The date on which the model is released
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on frontier safety frameworks.

options.html: The law that requires the framework's publication
options.text: The law that requires the framework's publication
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on frontier safety frameworks.

forms.stemHtml: An outside evaluator is given three days with a finished model and no information about how it was trained. Why does this limit what the evaluation can show?

options.html: Outside evaluators aren't permitted to publish results
options.text: Outside evaluators aren't permitted to publish results
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how commitments are checked.

options.html: Finished models can't be tested for dangerous abilities
options.text: Finished models can't be tested for dangerous abilities
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how commitments are checked.

options.html: Only government institutes may test models
options.text: Only government institutes may test models
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how commitments are checked.

options.html: What an evaluator learns depends on its access
options.text: What an evaluator learns depends on its access
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Access means what an outside party is permitted to see and test, and for how long. Less access means a weaker check.

forms.stemHtml: Two groups criticize AI companies' safety commitments from opposite directions. Which statements belong to the criticism that commitments are too weak? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Open release lets outsiders inspect a model
options.text: Open release lets outsiders inspect a model
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on each criticism of self-governance.

options.html: Companies revise promises when rivals don't follow them
options.text: Companies revise promises when rivals don't follow them
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! These critics argue that competitive pressure makes a voluntary commitment weakest when a rival is about to get ahead.

options.html: An outside scorecard gave no company a high grade
options.text: An outside scorecard gave no company a high grade
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A 2026 safety index graded no company above C+. Its publisher campaigns for stronger regulation.

options.html: Safety talk helps incumbents block small rivals
options.text: Safety talk helps incumbents block small rivals
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on each criticism of self-governance.

forms.stemHtml: What is a summit declaration on AI mainly useful for?

options.html: Recording what governments said together
options.text: Recording what governments said together
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A declaration records shared statements, gives officials and campaigners a text to cite, and can prepare the ground for something firmer.

options.html: Setting penalties for unsafe AI companies
options.text: Setting penalties for unsafe AI companies
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on summits and declarations.

options.html: Replacing national laws in signing countries
options.text: Replacing national laws in signing countries
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on summits and declarations.

options.html: Creating inspectors with access to AI labs
options.text: Creating inspectors with access to AI labs
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on summits and declarations.

forms.stemHtml: An expert body publishes a yearly report stating what the evidence shows about AI's risks. A government ignores the report. What follows?

options.html: The body can impose sanctions on the government
options.text: The body can impose sanctions on the government
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on scientific and treaty bodies.

options.html: The report becomes law after one year
options.text: The report becomes law after one year
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on scientific and treaty bodies.

options.html: The government loses its seat on the body
options.text: The government loses its seat on the body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on scientific and treaty bodies.

options.html: Nothing, since an assessment doesn't bind
options.text: Nothing, since an assessment doesn't bind
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Scientific assessments supply a shared account of the evidence. They set no rules and bind no one.

forms.stemHtml: A government restricts the sale of advanced AI chips to a rival country. What is this kind of rule called?

options.html: A usage restriction
options.text: A usage restriction
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on security competition.

options.html: A framework convention
options.text: A framework convention
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on security competition.

options.html: An export control
options.text: An export control
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An export control is a government rule that restricts the sale of certain goods or technology to other countries.

options.html: A prohibited practice
options.text: A prohibited practice
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on security competition.

forms.stemHtml: The Red Cross has proposed new rules on autonomous weapons. Which of these are part of its position? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Rule out systems whose effects can't be predicted
options.text: Rule out systems whose effects can't be predicted
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The position says unpredictable autonomous weapon systems should be expressly ruled out.

options.html: Leave the matter to each military's own policy
options.text: Leave the matter to each military's own policy
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on military use and autonomous weapons.

options.html: Rule out their use to target human beings
options.text: Rule out their use to target human beings
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The position says use of autonomous weapon systems to target human beings should be ruled out.

options.html: Regulate the rest with limits and human supervision
options.text: Regulate the rest with limits and human supervision
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Other systems would be limited by target, duration, area, and scale, with human supervision and timely intervention.

forms.stemHtml: Which statement best describes risk-based regulation as the EU's AI Act applies it?

options.html: Heavier duties for uses that could do more harm
options.text: Heavier duties for uses that could do more harm
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The Act bans a short list of uses, sets strict duties for high-risk uses, requires transparency for some, and sets no new rules for the rest.

options.html: The same duties for every AI system on the market
options.text: The same duties for every AI system on the market
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the European Union's risk-based law.

options.html: A ban on AI until each system is proven safe
options.text: A ban on AI until each system is proven safe
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the European Union's risk-based law.

options.html: Duties that apply only to the largest AI models
options.text: Duties that apply only to the largest AI models
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the European Union's risk-based law.

forms.stemHtml: Why can US federal policy on AI change quickly when a new president takes office?

options.html: Federal AI statutes expire every four years
options.text: Federal AI statutes expire every four years
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the United States.

options.html: State laws lapse when the presidency changes
options.text: State laws lapse when the presidency changes
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the United States.

options.html: Courts must review AI policy after each election
options.text: Courts must review AI policy after each election
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the United States.

options.html: It rests on orders a president can revoke
options.text: It rests on orders a president can revoke
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An executive order is a directive from the president that needs no vote in Congress, and a later president can revoke it, as happened to the 2023 order in January 2025.

forms.stemHtml: A reader works from an English translation of China's AI measures. Which cautions apply? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The Chinese text is the one with legal force
options.text: The Chinese text is the one with legal force
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The English wording comes from an independent translation project.

options.html: The text doesn't show how strictly rules are enforced
options.text: The text doesn't show how strictly rules are enforced
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Terms such as "public opinion properties" leave wide discretion to officials, and enforcement can't be read from the text.

options.html: The measures are voluntary guidance for companies
options.text: The measures are voluntary guidance for companies
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on China.

options.html: The same rules also serve the state's control of information
options.text: The same rules also serve the state's control of information
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Labeling and data rules address widely shared problems, and content rules tie AI services to the state's control of information.

forms.stemHtml: Several AI developers publish frameworks that tie safeguards to capability thresholds. Who writes a framework and decides whether one of its thresholds has been reached?

options.html: A government safety institute
options.text: A government safety institute
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on frontier safety frameworks.

options.html: The hosts of the Seoul summit
options.text: The hosts of the Seoul summit
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on frontier safety frameworks.

options.html: An independent panel of experts
options.text: An independent panel of experts
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on frontier safety frameworks.

options.html: The company itself
options.text: The company itself
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A framework is a company's statement of what it will do. The company writes it, judges whether a threshold has been reached, and can revise it.

forms.stemHtml: A company announces that outside reviewers will work inside it with standing access and the right to publish. No law requires this. What weakness remains?

options.html: The access still rests on the company's consent
options.text: The access still rests on the company's consent
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Access that a company grants voluntarily can be narrowed or withdrawn unless a law requires it.

options.html: The reviewers would be government employees
options.text: The reviewers would be government employees
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how commitments are checked.

options.html: The reviewers couldn't see any internal information
options.text: The reviewers couldn't see any internal information
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how commitments are checked.

options.html: The arrangement would violate whistleblower laws
options.text: The arrangement would violate whistleblower laws
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how commitments are checked.

forms.stemHtml: The "too weak" critics and the "regulatory capture" critics disagree about binding rules. On which points do they agree? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A company's own account of its safety shouldn't be taken on trust
options.text: A company's own account of its safety shouldn't be taken on trust
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Both groups distrust what companies say about themselves.

options.html: Binding safety rules should be adopted quickly
options.text: Binding safety rules should be adopted quickly
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on each criticism of self-governance.

options.html: Who gains from a position is worth asking
options.text: Who gains from a position is worth asking
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Both critiques ask who benefits: one from weak commitments, the other from rules that burden rivals.

options.html: Open-weight models should be restricted
options.text: Open-weight models should be restricted
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on each criticism of self-governance.

forms.stemHtml: A headline reads: "World agrees binding AI safety rules at summit." The summit produced a declaration. What is wrong with the headline?

options.html: Summits can't discuss AI safety at all
options.text: Summits can't discuss AI safety at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on summits and declarations.

options.html: Only companies can sign declarations
options.text: Only companies can sign declarations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on summits and declarations.

options.html: Declarations apply only to the host country
options.text: Declarations apply only to the host country
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on summits and declarations.

options.html: A declaration binds no one
options.text: A declaration binds no one
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A declaration is a joint statement of what governments believe or intend. It creates no legal duty.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these can create legal duties for a country regarding AI?

options.html: An annual report from a UN scientific panel
options.text: An annual report from a UN scientific panel
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on scientific and treaty bodies.

options.html: An expert safety report backed by thirty countries
options.text: An expert safety report backed by thirty countries
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on scientific and treaty bodies.

options.html: A treaty the country has ratified, once in force
options.text: A treaty the country has ratified, once in force
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Assessments inform and don't bind. A treaty binds the countries that ratify it, once enough have done so for it to take effect.

options.html: A statement issued at the close of a summit
options.text: A statement issued at the close of a summit
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on scientific and treaty bodies.

forms.stemHtml: Some argue that rival powers can coordinate on AI because they limited nuclear weapons during the Cold War. What does the historical record establish?

options.html: Nothing, since those treaties all failed
options.text: Nothing, since those treaties all failed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on security competition.

options.html: That AI can be verified as missiles were
options.text: That AI can be verified as missiles were
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on security competition.

options.html: That rivals never honor agreements
options.text: That rivals never honor agreements
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on security competition.

options.html: That rivals have coordinated before
options.text: That rivals have coordinated before
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The record shows that rivals have limited dangerous technologies, imperfectly and with verification. Whether those methods carry over to AI is a forecast.

forms.stemHtml: In 2026 a dispute arose between the US Defense Department and an AI supplier over a usage restriction. Which statements describe a usage restriction? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It's a limit a supplier writes into its contract or terms
options.text: It's a limit a supplier writes into its contract or terms
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A usage restriction is set by the supplier.

options.html: It concerns what a customer may do with a product
options.text: It concerns what a customer may do with a product
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It limits the uses a customer may make of what it has bought or licensed.

options.html: It's a ban agreed by states in a treaty
options.text: It's a ban agreed by states in a treaty
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on military use and autonomous weapons.

options.html: It's a government rule on sales to other countries
options.text: It's a government rule on sales to other countries
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on military use and autonomous weapons.

title: Governance and Regulation
